messages:
maria: Hey team — customer hit an embeddings/rerank mismatch when sending batched requests. They say some vectors are length 1536 and some are length 0. Seen it twice in prod for customer acct acct_7G4. Request IDs attached: req_01F7aX9, req_01F7aY2. Posting the pasted curl they used below.

alex: thanks — can you drop the raw curl and one of the failing request IDs into a debug bundle? also need timestamps from their side (client send). any chance this is client-side gzip or chunking weirdness? :thinking:

maria: here's the curl they used (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXXX' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-binary '{"model":"rwd-embed-compact-2","input":["doc1 text...","doc2 text...","doc3 text...","doc4 text...","doc5 text...","doc6 text...","doc7 text...","doc8 text..."]}'
```
They said they gzip the body in their client (requests library) and set Content-Encoding: gzip. Their reported client send time for req_01F7aX9 was 2025-11-12T18:21:07Z.

lin: I'm pulling logs for req_01F7aX9 and req_01F7aY2. quick note: I see a reshape warning in batcher-3 around 18:21:08Z. Sample server log: 
```
[2025-11-12T18:21:08Z] batcher-3 WARN reshape: input_count mismatch (expected 8, got 7) correlation=req_01F7aX9 worker=batcher-3
[2025-11-12T18:21:08Z] batcher-3 ERROR kv-cache: missing-kv for request req_01F7aX9 shard=4
[2025-11-12T18:21:08Z] router INFO route-fallback model=rwd-embed-compact-2 -> rwd-embed-compact-2-quant correlation=req_01F7aX9
```
Looks like one item was not parsed by the batching layer. Could be a trailing null byte after gzip or a content-length mismatch.

maria: customer says the client library retries on transient 5xx and serializes arrays using numpy which sometimes inserts a stray None for empty docs. they insisted there were 8 strings though.

alex: two immediate asks: 1) can you upload a debug bundle for both req IDs (logs, raw request body captured by ingress, and the batcher dump)? 2) ask customer to re-run with --compressed removed (i.e., no gzip) and report. If they can't, ask for a small reproducible payload (2-3 items).

support-bot: debug bundle for req_01F7aX9 uploaded -> https://s3.redwood-internal/debug/1755554321_req_01F7aX9.tar.gz (logs + ingress raw + batcher snapshot).

lin: I inspected the ingress raw from the bundle. The ingress captured Content-Length: 1024 but body length = 1019 bytes after gunzip. There are 5 trailing bytes lost in the pipe read on the proxy side. That would truncate the JSON array tail and cause the parser to drop the last element. Pasted ingress snippet: 
```
{"model":"rwd-embed-compact-2","input":["doc1","doc2","doc3","doc4","doc5","doc6","doc7","doc8"]}

(gunzip -> truncated to ..."doc7","doc8"]}
```
So the proxy read loop returned earlier. Investigating proxy config for keepalive/limit.

maria: customer also attached a smaller repro where they sent 3 items and saw same issue, request id req_01F7bZ0. they shared a minimal curl: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXXX' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Content-Encoding: gzip' \
  --data-binary @payload.json.gz
```
payload.json contents before gz: {"model":"rwd-embed-compact-2","input":["a","b","c"]}

lin: grabbed that bundle too. In that case the proxy chunking logic dropped the last 2 bytes when Content-Length didn't match compressed-size header from client library. There's a known bug in older nginx tcp buffer patches where compressed payload length can be mis-calculated when client closes early.

alex: OK diagnosis sounds like: client gzips -> proxy read returns short -> JSON truncated -> batcher sees fewer items -> reshape mismatch -> some vectors absent. Plan: 1) workaround for customer: turn off gzip or send smaller batches. 2) server fix: add stricter ingress validation to reject mismatch between Content-Length and actual bytes and return 400 instead of truncating. 3) longer term: patch proxy read loop to stream until EOF.

maria: I've told the customer to toggle off Content-Encoding and re-run the small 3-item repro; asked for new request id. asked them to include exact client library version (they're on requests 2.31.0 + python 3.11).

lin: filed ENG-INF ticket INF-3821 to add ingress validation + hard fail on truncated request, assigning to eng-infra. linked logs and bundles.

ingest-bot: ENG-INF ticket created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3821 (assignee: @samir)

maria: customer ran the non-gzip 3-item test and confirmed success (req_01F7cM9). they also ran the original 8-item with gzip and it failed again (req_01F7dN2). so workaround validated.

alex: good. next steps for support: 1) mark as workaround advised and escalate to infra for patch. 2) set follow-up to confirm infra fix and then notify customer for re-test. I'll add a support ticket note summarizing. :white_check_mark:

maria: thanks all — closing temporary loop, will keep thread updated when INF-3821 lands. :pray:
